newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MHS may pull out of Cambodia airline.
newsitem.headline: MHS may pull out of Cambodia airline.

text.p: Malaysian Helicopter Services Bhd (MHS) may pull out of its investment in Royal Air Cambodge (RAC) if Cambodia implements its open skies policy, domestic newspapers reported on Friday.

"If the open skies policy is implemented, there would be no reason for increasing equity in RAC and a pull-out may also be considered," The Star daily quoted MHS chairman Tajudin Ramli as telling reporters on Thursday.
Tajudin said final decision on the issue would be left to directors of MHS and RAC. MHS officials were not immediately available for comment.
MHS holds a 40 percent stake in RAC and the Cambodian government the remaining 60 percent.
Malaysian Airline System Bhd, also led by Tajudin, has a management contract with the Cambodian national carrier.
MHS owns a 29.1 percent equity in Malaysian Airlines.

Cambodia's First Prime Minister Hun Sen said on Monday he was in favour of an "open skies policy" with regard to the airline industry as he sought to calm foreign investors after ousting First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh.
